content.content:
# Performance

## Description

The cost of the tree system is measured in the running game, not guessed. The hand-made trees are gone, so the cost is measured against the same stage with no trees.

## Counters

- A tree stats overlay, shown with the [Lod.debugView](./Lod.md#debug-view) toggle, reports per frame the number of trees drawn at each level and in a fade, the triangles and draw calls of the tree passes, shadow passes included, and the GPU time of the tree main pass and tree shadow pass on their own.
- It also reports the CPU time of level selection and fade updates per frame.
- At stage load it records the time spent deriving, meshing and baking variants, how many came from the disk cache, and the GPU and disk memory the variants use.

## Benchmark

- A benchmark runs a fixed camera path along a stage with the procedural trees and reports the average, 1% low and worst frame time, the tree GPU time and the stage load time.
- It can run the same path with trees turned off, so the trees' own cost is the difference between the two runs.
- Results are written to a file with the stage, graphics quality setting, resolution and GPU, so runs can be compared.

## Hotspots

- Alpha-tested foliage overdraw near the camera, made larger by the 120 m full-detail distance.
- The two levels drawn together during a fade.
- Shadow casters, drawn again for each cascade.
- Stage load on a cold cache, when every variant and impostor is generated.
## Debug View

A debug toggle tints each tree by the level it draws, shows trees in a fade with the fade value, and marks trees that changed level more than twice in the last second, so flickering trees can be found in a running stage.

content.text:
It's a big hit: the trees take a stable frame of about 2.6 ms up to 21–34 ms, below 60 fps and on one stage below 30. Almost all of it is GPU drawing time, not the L-system. I measured it with the stats overlay and benchmark the spec asked for, on this machine's AMD Radeon 890M (integrated graphics) at medium quality, 1280×720.

The spec step again said `src/` was empty. It isn't, so I built the tools into the existing game.

| Per frame | Petralica | The Jackie |
|---|---|---|
| Average frame without trees | 2.6 ms | 2.8 ms |
| Average frame with trees | 20.9 ms | 33.8 ms |
| **Trees' own cost** | **+18.3 ms** | **+31.0 ms** |
| GPU time of the tree passes | 12.8 ms | 26.4 ms |
| 1% low (99th percentile frame) with trees | 32 ms | 206 ms |
| Worst frame with trees | 1.27 s | 1.65 s |
| Worst frame without trees | 11 ms | 9 ms |

**Where the time goes,** from the overlay at the start of The Jackie:
- **Main pass:** about 13 million tree triangles in 306 draw calls, about 21 ms of GPU time. The middle detail level is the biggest share: 7,620 trees at roughly 1,800 triangles each.
- **Shadow pass:** about 10 million triangles, but only about 3.4 ms of GPU time.
- **Fades, CPU and draw calls:** fades are negligible (0 trees were fading in that frame). Level selection costs about 1 ms of CPU per frame. Draw calls stay around 300, so they aren't the problem.
- **Loading:** on a cold cache, generating and baking all 24 variants took about 0.6 s, of which generation about 0.24 s and impostor baking about 0.36 s. That's a small part of the 6–13 s stage load. The variants use about 70 MB of GPU memory and 61 MB of disk cache.

**Stutters:** the 1–1.6 s worst frames and Jackie's 206 ms 1% low only happen with trees on. I haven't tracked down the cause. My guess is new tree batches being created or growing their buffers mid-run, rather than steady drawing cost.

The main cause is that the much further detail distances from the last change leave thousands of trees as full geometry. Bringing those thresholds closer, or making the middle level much lighter, would cut most of this cost. That's a spec decision for you.

What I built:
- **Stats overlay:** shown with the LOD debug view, toggled by the new F6 key in the game or the existing checkbox in the map viewer. Per frame it shows:
  - trees at each level, fading and flickering
  - draw calls, triangles and GPU time for the tree main pass and the tree shadow pass separately
  - CPU time of level selection and of the batching job
  - load cost: generation and bake time, cache hits, GPU and disk memory
- **Benchmark:** open `/games/rally/?map=<id>&treebench=1`, or run `await __rally.treeBenchmark()` in the console. The camera flies a fixed 600 m from the stage start, first with trees and then without.
  - It reports average, 1% low and worst frame time, tree GPU time and load time, with the stage, quality, resolution and GPU.
  - Each frame waits for the GPU to finish, so vsync can't hide the cost.
  - It downloads the results as `tree-bench-<stage>-<quality>-<resolution>-<date>.json`. My runs above read the results directly instead, because downloads don't work in the headless browser.

Type check, lint and all 496 tests pass, and `DETAILS.md` is updated. The new code is in `trees/stats.ts`, `trees/overlay.ts` and `game/tree-bench.ts`. Nothing is committed.
